items.summary: Driving the MCP playtest is now a standing responsibility of the rpg-dnd5e-web team-member.
items.description: As of 2026-05-30 Wave 0 signoff, the web team-member operates the MCP playtest harness end-to-end via Chrome DevTools MCP (port 9222). The playtest is the wave signoff bar — CI-green is necessary but not sufficient. Setup: (1) kill old servers, (2) start rpg-api with AUTH_DEV_MODE=true, (3) start Envoy proxy via Docker (--network host, envoy/envoy.yaml proxies :8080 → :50051), (4) clear .vite cache + start npm run dev on rpg-dnd5e-web, (5) seed fixture via go run ./cmd/devseed --fixture=<name>. Navigate to /playtest?encounterId=<id>&playerId=<player>.

items.summary: rpg-api runs gRPC on :50051; web needs an Envoy proxy on :8080 for gRPC-Web. Envoy must run before the playtest.
items.description: The web client (Connect-ES) sends HTTP/gRPC-Web requests to localhost:8080. The API server only speaks raw gRPC on :50051. Envoy translates. The config lives at rpg-api/envoy/envoy.yaml. With Docker available: `docker run -d --name rpg-envoy --network host -v /home/kirk/personal/rpg-api/envoy/envoy.yaml:/etc/envoy/envoy.yaml envoyproxy/envoy:v1.31-latest -c /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml`. Use --network host so Envoy can reach localhost:50051.

items.summary: wave-3-barbarian fixture uses random initiative (enc.SetMode(ModeTurnBased) rolls dice). For playtests where player-first order matters, manipulate Redis or add a fixture flag.
items.description: The devseed fixture calls enc.SetMode(ModeTurnBased) which rolls random initiative. In the 2026-05-30 playtest, goblin won initiative (goblin → char-bob), blocking the playtest flow since there's no web UI to skip the goblin's first turn. Fix: redis-cli GET enc:v2:dev-encounter | python3 -c 'd["initiative"]=["char-bob","goblin-1"]; d["active_idx"]=0; print(json.dumps(d))' | redis-cli -x SET enc:v2:dev-encounter. Long-term fix: add --force-bob-first flag to devseed, or add a SetInitiativeOrder method to the encounter SDK.

items.summary: A missed attack (TakeAction RPC succeeds, d20 roll < AC) produces no EntityDamaged stream event and no web feedback. The event log shows TakeAction(attack) with no follow-up.
items.description: With random dice, bob (+5 to hit vs goblin AC 15) has ~55% hit chance. A miss fires only AttackResolvedEvent (suppressed by translate.go as cause-only with no wire shape). DamageDealtEvent only fires on hit. Result: from the web's perspective, a miss looks identical to a 'pending' state — the event log shows the RPC call but nothing else. First attack in the 2026-05-30 playtest was a miss; second hit. This is a known gap — no miss indication to the player.

items.summary: Audit corrections must propagate to every doc occurrence, not just discoveries — grep all docs.
items.description: When an audit catches drift (line counts, file existence, API shape), the correction must propagate to ALL doc claims, not just where I first wrote it. Discoveries in context/ are not enough — grep -rn the docs for the stale fact and fix every occurrence. 'I noted it in discoveries' is not the same as 'the docs are correct.' PR #379 Copilot review found 13 comments all tracing back to this failure: context knew the right facts, but multiple doc files still claimed the old ones.

items.summary: Test counts must come from npm test summary line, not grep — status.md claimed 323 vs actual 298.
items.description: The status.md test count (323) was wrong. Grep for 'tests' in the vitest output is not reliable — run npm test and read the summary line. Actual: 298 tests, 14 files.

items.summary: Verify a commit is on main with git branch --contains before claiming it shipped.
items.description: Before claiming a commit is on main, run: git log --oneline origin/main | grep <hash>. Or: git branch --contains <hash>. The 15f232e commit was only on the PR branch.

items.summary: Always re-grep legacy comment count in LobbyView.tsx live; cached numbers go stale fast.
items.description: The legacy comment count changes as refactoring happens. Always grep -c 'legacy' src/components/LobbyView.tsx rather than relying on a cached number. Was 41 at PR #379 creation, 26 on current branch as of 2026-05-02.

items.summary: When proto events carry both 'rich' (entity snapshot) and 'thin' (path/id) fields, the consumer must accept either shape — the server can legitimately send only one.
items.description: MovementCompletedEvent has updatedEntity (full snapshot) AND path[]+entityId (delta-shaped). The API on player moves currently sends only the delta-shaped fields; on monster moves it sends both. The web consumer originally only acted when updatedEntity was set, so player moves silently dropped on the floor. Lesson: when the proto exposes overlapping/redundant fields, the consumer should treat them as a fallback chain, not a single required field. Mirror what the matched producer-side path does — applyMonsterMovement already used path[last]; handleMovementCompleted should too. Found 2026-05-05 during Wave 2 cross-room state work.
